name: Vegetarian Tteokbokki
steps: Check the rice-cake packet for animal-derived ingredients and use plain cylindrical cakes. If frozen, thaw; if firm, soak in cool water for 10 minutes and drain. Separate any cakes stuck together.
Simmer the measured 750 ml water with dried kelp and the white parts of the spring onions for 8 minutes. Remove the kelp so the broth stays clear and does not become bitter.
Whisk gochujang, gochugaru, brown rice syrup and soy sauce into the hot kelp broth until the paste dissolves. Bring to a gentle boil and add the drained rice cakes.

Simmer uncovered for 8–12 minutes, stirring frequently so rice cakes do not stick to the pan, until the cakes are soft and chewy and their starch thickens the sauce. If the pan dries before they soften, add a splash of hot water.

Turn off the heat and stir in sesame oil. Divide into four warm bowls, spoon the thick red sauce over the rice cakes and top with green spring onion and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately while the cakes are supple.
tips: Use kelp water rather than anchovy stock and omit fish cakes. The reviewed photo shows short cylindrical rice cakes in thick red gochujang sauce, scallions and sesame only.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
